research.title: How Aaru Uses Advanced AI Simulations to Predict Human Behavior
research.summary: Aaru, a two-and-a-half-year-old startup valued at $1 billion, is redefining market research and consumer intelligence by deploying multi-agent AI simulations to predict how humans will make decisions. Cam Fink, co-founder and CEO, and Ned Koh, co-founder and president, discuss Aaru's founding story and how advanced behavioral simulation overcomes the limitations of traditional consumer polling. In this conversation with Goldman Sachs Chief Information Officer Marco Argenti, they also explore the real-world enterprise applications of such predictive simulations across retail, financial services, and utilities, which are driving Aaru's rapid rise.

research.title: John Waldron on GDP Growth, AI, and the M&A Outlook
research.summary: Goldman Sachs President and COO John Waldron says clients have a cautiously optimistic outlook and the surge in M&A is a sign of that confidence. In the Exchanges podcast, he also discusses opportunities in asset and wealth management and how AI can help the firm serve clients better.

research.title: Midterm Election Results: Three Key Takeaways
research.summary: Democrats delivered a stronger-than-expected performance in the midterms. Our Head of Public Policy Research Ariana Salvatore examines what the results could mean for Washington’s policy priorities, the balance of political power and the investment landscape. Read more insights from Morgan Stanley.

research.title: Capital is tilting East: Inside Asia’s AI gold rush
research.summary: Southeast Asia’s economy has grown nearly ninefold since 1998, and the region is now at the center of the global AI investment cycle. In this episode of Making Sense, Sjoerd Leenart, CEO of J.P. Morgan’s banking business in Asia Pacific, sits down with Joyce Chang, chair of Global Research at J.P. Morgan, to unpack key takeaways from the investor seminar hosted around the IMF–World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok. They discuss the forces propelling Asia’s growth — from the manufacturing renaissance driven by AI data center demand to divergent policy tailwinds across China, Japan, Korea and ASEAN economies. They also explore the IMF’s latest global outlook, the narrowing base of countries driving world growth and why investor sentiment has shifted from "fear of missing out" to more…
